Insurance Commn., Mar., 1913 to June, 1914; assigned to C.O., June, 1914; on military service from Aug., 1914 to Jan., 1919; col. audt. dept., 1919; asst. audr., Gold Coast, Jan., 1920; do., Sierra Leone, Feb., 1923; do., Gold Coast, Nov., 1931; ag. dep. audr., various occasions, 1931-33; senr. asst. audr., Nigeria, 1934.

FOSTER, Robert Spence, M.A. (Oxon.)—B. 1891; ed. Magdalen Coll. Schl. and St. Edmund Hall, Oxford; 2nd lieut., K.S.L.I., 1915; K.A.R., 1917-19; head mast., educ., Tanganyika Territory, 1922; ag. dir., educ., Aug. to Oct., 1924; Swahili examr.; dep. dir., educ., Uganda, 1930; ag. dir., educ., in 1931, 1934 and 1935.

FOSTER, William, O.B.E. (1935), M.B.E.—B. 1880; served in S. African War, 1900-02; Queen's Med., 3 clasps; King's Med., 2 clasps; Br. post office, 1897-1920; serv. in Gt. War, 1914-20; ment. in desps.; major, 1920; dep. postmtr.-gen., Palestine, July, 1920; ag. postmtr.-gen., on several occasions.

FOULGER, Harry Cecil, M.A. (1928)—B. 1891; ed. Malvern Coll. and Pembroke Coll., Camb.; capt., R. Fusiliers; asst. res., Nyasaland Prot., Aug., 1914; attd., K.A.R., ag. pvte. sec. and A.D.C. to gov., 1919; res., 1st grade, Jan., 1924; ag. prov. commnr., Jan.-Sept., 1935.

FOUND, William Ambrose, D.Sc.—B. 1873; ed pub. schls. and Prince of Wales Coll., Prince Ed. Island; dept. marine and fisheries, Canada, 1898; supt., fisheries in combined dept., 1911; advr. to Br. plenipotentiaries when pelagic sealing treaty negotiated, 1911; mem., Canadian-American Fisheries Commn., 1918; dep. min., fisheries, 1928.

FOURIE, The Hon. A. P. J.—Formerly mem., Cape prov. coun. and subsequently mem., H. of A. for Somerset; M.H.A., Gordonia; admstr., Prov. of the Cape of Good Hope, Jan., 1926; min. of mines and industries, Aug., 1929; del., Imp. Confec., London, 1930 and del., Ottawa Econ. Confec., 1932; min., lab., commerce and industries, Apr., 1933.

FOURIE, Louis, M.B.E.—B. 1878; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch, Edin. Univ.; Berlin; M.B., Ch.B. (Hons) (Conan Doyle Prizeman); D.P.H., F.Z.S., F.R.A.I., Fell. Soc. M.O.H., M.R. San. Inst., mem., Amer. Anthropol. Assocn., res. med. offr., R. Infirmary, 1905; city fever hosp., 1906; roy. hosp. sick. child., Edin., 1906-7; h.-surgeon, Paddington Green Child. hosp., Lond., 1907; act. serv., Boer Forces, 1899-1900; D.S. Taunsg, 1913-15; capt., S.A.M.C., 1916-19; M.O. to admstr., S.W.A., 1920-29; asst. health offr., Union Health Dep., 1930.

FOWLIS, Henry George—Entd. judl. dept., Gambia, 1890; gov't. off., 1893-1901; col. sec.'s off., 1902-06; ch. clk. and acctnt., P.W.D., 1906.

FOX, Harold Robert Leslie, B.Sc. (Mass.), A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1889; Institute of Technology; served in Great War, 1915-19; ment. in desps., demob. with rank of capt., 1919; ch. engrnr., Jamaica govt. rly., 1926; ag. dir., June-Sept., 1931.

FOXLEE, Richard William, M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1885; ed. Westminster Schl.; served in rail. dept., G.N.R., 1903-09; G.C.R., 1909-15; F.L.R., 1915-21; dep. head, engrnr. design dept., 1921; dep. ch. engrnr. (civ.), 1928.

FRAMPTON, Algernon deKewer, C.D.A.—B. 1904; ed. Christ's Hosp., Oxford Schl.; Economics and at Wye Agrl. Coll.; Imp. Trop. Agr., Trinidad, 1926; ag. offr. agr., Nigeria, 1927; agrl. supt., Br. Guiana, 1929.

FRANCE, Henry Dunlop.—Rev. of Anguilla, 1896; govt. offr., St. Kitts, 1917; rev. offr., Nevis, 1899; tariff clk., rev. of St. Kitts, 1901; ag. audit clk., St. Kitts, 1902; supervisor of cust., G. Coast, Sept., 1917; clk. supervisor of cust., Aug., 1919; ag. cust. preven. serv., Mar.—Oct., 1911; ag. maritime cust., Oct., 1916 to Jan., 1917; collr. cust., Jan., 1921.

FRANCIS, Clifford Claude, Barr-at-Law, Lincoln's Inn.—B. 1889; ed. at Keble Schl., Rochester, and Lincoln Coll.; on service in Fiji, 1908-12; cadet W. Pacific (Br. Solomon Is. Prot.), June, 1912; passed May, 1914; dep. commnr., high constab., Dec., 1914; lieut., E. Surrey Regt., May; capt., Apr., 1916; served in France and Fland., 1917-18; dist. offr., Gizo, Br. Solomon Is., 1919; ag. res. commnr. of Prot., Oct., 1920; Mar., 1923; rep. natives of Gizo dist. before lands commn., 1923; judl. commn. for Pacific in New Hebrides and Br. judge, for New Hebrides condominium, Aug., 1925; mag., Nigeria, 1930; puisne judge, Uga., and mem., ct. of appl. for Eastern Africa, 1934; ag. ch. just., Aug.-Oct., 1934.

FRANCIS, Cyril Gerard Brooke (1934)—Apptd. Fiji civ. serv., 1898; lieu. nat. constab., 1901; certif., musketeer, machine gun, Hythe, 1905; called to the bar, Temple, 1907; inspr., Fiji constab., barrister and solr., sup. ct., Fiji, 1908; ag. to ag. gov., for various periods, 1908-10; grade dist. commnr., May, 1912; 2nd in local forces with rank of major, Aug., 1914; by Army Council for services in 1914 in connection with defence of Fiji; capt., E. Surrey Regt., Mar., 1915; ovv. commr., K.A.R., Africa, 1916-19; 1st grade dist. commnr., Jan., 1916; regir.-gen., regir., sup. ct., ex-stamps, and pub. trustee, Fiji, Jan., 1920; enemy property and contr. L.C.O., Fiji-Pacific, Feb., 1920; ag. atty.-gen., May, 1921; commr. for the revision of the laws of Fiji, 1920 (not completed); atty.-gen., Honduras, July, 1921; ag. ch. just., 1922 and 1923; chmn., commn. to ensure outbreak of yellow fever, 1921; chmn., government commn., 1922; chmn., franchise commn., 1923; revd. and consol. law, B. Hond., atty.-gen., Zanzibar, Nov., 1924; atty.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, 1929; judge, high court, N. Rhodesia, Nov., 1934.

FRANCIS, Josiah.—Served European war with A.I.F., 1916-19; M.H.R., (wealth Australia since 1922; hon. min., Lyons' min., 1932.

FRANKS, John William, O.B.E. (1881)-1879; prison commn., H.O., June, 1889; asst. supt., Victoria Gaol, Hong Kong, Nov., 1897; asst. supt. pol. res., Feb., 1929; supt. pres., Dec., 1920.
FRASER, ALASTAIR GARDEN, B.A.—B. 1902; Rugby and Queen's Coll., Oxford; B.A., '4; 3rd cls. hons., phil., polit., and econ.; c.t. mast., Achimota, Gold Coast, 1924.

FRASER, REV. ALEXANDER GARDEN, C.B.E. (1830), M.A.—B. 1873; ed. Merchiston Castle, in., Edin. Univ. and Trinity Coll., Oxford; assn., 1913; priest, 1915; C.M.S., Uganda, 1903; prin., Trinity Coll., Kandy, Ceylon, '4; chaplain with 3rd divn., France, 1917-18; aplain to the forces; prin., Prince of Wales ll., Achimota, Gold Coast, 1924.

FRASER, D. M.—B.1890; Br. post office, 1906; st. clk. and telegraphist, Kenya and Uganda, 13; postmr., Tanganyika, 1917; ch. acct., postal d'tels., 1919; ast. P.M.G., Keyna, 1933; ret., 34; ast. P.M.G., Trinidad, 1936.

FRASER, H.—Ed. Grammar Sch., Inveraray; Jorge Watson's Coll., Edinburgh and Edinburgh Univ.; B.Sc., 1925; ast. conservator of forests, anganyika Territory, 1925.

FRASER, HUGH., B.A.—B. 1890; ed. Wellington and Exeter Coll., Oxford(schol.); cadet, F.M.S., 13; ag. priv. sec. to ch. sec., Apr., 1914-Feb., 15; ag. supervisor of cust., Port Dickson, May, 15; ditto, Port Swettenham, Jan., 1916; ast. cadet, Dec., 1916; offr., cls. V., Dec., 1916; d ast. sec., Fed. sect., Aug., 1917, priv. sec. to sec. in admn., Sept., 1917; dist. offr., Jelebu, sh., 1918; ast. dist. offr., Ipoh, Sept., 1920; fr., cls. IV., Nov., 1920; 3rd ast. sec. to govt., M.S., Dec., 1920; dist. offr., Kuantan, Sept., 24; offr., class III., Nov., 1925; ag. ast. advr., edah, Mar., 1927; ag. temp. legal adviser, edah in admn., Apr. to Dec., 1927; ag. ast. eases., F.M.S. and state treas., Selangor, June, 129; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1930; dist. offr., Larut ad regis., titles, Perak, Nov., 1930; offg. mag., Lumbur, Nov., 1932; ag. sec. to res., Perak, lar., 1933; offr. cls. I.B., 1934; Malayan estab., ftr., Mar., 1936; sec., high commr. in admn., Aug., 336.

FRASER, JOHN ALEXANDER, M.C., Barrister-at-Law.—B. 1896; ed. Trinity Academy, with, and Edin. Univ.; on mil. serv., 1915-19; adet., Hong Kong, 1919; addl. to sany. dept., 921; 3rd ast. to sec. for Chinese affrs., 1921; nd pol. mag., Apr., 1922; dist. offr. (North), June, 1922; passed in Cantonese, 1922; ast. cad., sany. dept. and sec. to sany. bd., 1922; ist. offr., South, 1924; ast. supt., impts. and xpts., 1925; dist. offr., North, Feb., 1926; dist. ffr., North and South Sept., 1928; called to bar, Middle Temple, June, 1931; pol. mag., Kowloon, July, 1931; ag. ast. atty.-gen., Oct., 1932; ag. crown solr., Aug., 1936.

FRASER, SIR JOHN GEORGE, KT. BACH. (1924), C.M.G. (1913).—B. 1884; cadet Ceylon iv. ser., Oct., 1887; ag. dist. judge, &c., Badulla, Feb., 1894; ast. govt. agt., Chilaw, Dec., 1899; and settm. offr., Aug., 1901; ag. govt. agt., W. Prov., 4th Jan., 1912; ag. controller of revenue, in 1911, 1912, 1913, 1915 and 1916; govt. agt., W. Prov., July, 1914; M.L.C.; ret., 1924.

FRASER, HON. PETER.—B. 1884; ed. Board Schl. and Workers' Educnl. Assn.; mem. of N.Z. H. of R. since 1918; represented N.Z. at Empire Parly. Confce., London, 1935; min. of educ., min. of health and min. of marine, 1935.

FRASER, WINFORD BLACHE.—B. 1868; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1892; mag., St. Andrew, Trinidad, Jan., 1923; mag., Caroni, Nov., 1923; mag., St. George East, Dec., 1924.

FRASER, HON. ST FRANCIS VERNON, KT. BACH. (1935), M.A., LL.B.—B. 1880; ed. Nelson Coll., Otago Univ. Coll., and Canterbury Univ. Coll.; barrister and solr., stip. mag., 1911; chmn., N.Z. pub. serv. appeal bd., 1918; ast. pub. serv. comsrr., 1920; judge, ct. of arbit., 1921-35; chmn., dairy industry comsrr., 1934; dep. chmn., exec. comsrr. of agr., 1935 also ast. dir., marketing, 1936.

FREEMAN, BENJAMIN JOHN.—B. 1888; ed. Christ's Hosp., London, and Horsham; br. P.O., Oct., 1903—Dec., 1913; jnr. postal clk. and telegraphist, Kenya, Jan., 1913; 2nd cls. postmr., Apr., 1919; ast. ch. acctnt., Apr., 1918; 1st cls. postmr., Apr., 1920; dep. ch. acctnt., June, 1924; ast. P.M.G., July, 1931; snr. acctnt., S.S., Aug., 1932; contrlr., P. and T., Selangor and Pahang, Agr., 1933.

FREEMAN, GROFFREY JAMES.—B. 1889; ed. privately and in Clongoweswood Coll., Ireland; served in Royal Dublin Fusiliers and Royal Munster Fusiliers in the Great War, 1914-21; colls., cust., Gold Coast, 1922; senr. do., Feb., 1932.

FREESTON, LESLIE BRIAN, O.B.E. (1930).—B. 1892; ed. at Willaston Schi., Nantwich and Oxford; scholar New Coll., 1911-1919; 2nd cls., hons. mod., 1913; B.A. (war), 1919; on mil. ser., 17th Sept., 1914 to 8th Mar., 1919; temp. 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 10th Mar. to 15th July, 1919; appt. under reconstruction scheme, 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 16th July, 1919; ast. prin., 1st Apr., 1920; priv. sec. to perm. under-sec., 18th June, 1920; sent to Ceylon for temp. serv. as sec., salaries comsrr., 1921; ast. prin., 6th Dec., 1922; prin., 1st April, 1924; visited Bahamas and Br. Hond. on duty, 1927; seconded for serv. with Col. Development Advisory Comtee., 1st Feb., 1930; sec., E. African govts. confce. and to the high comsrr. for transp., Kenya and Uganda, Jan., 1936.

FREETH, ARTHUR CAUSTON.—B.1890; ed. Lancang Coll. (exhib.), St. Mary's Hosp. and Coll. of Med., Newcastle-on-Tyne, M.B., Dunelm, certif., London Schi. of Trop. Med.; temp. capt., R.A.M.C., 1915-20; med. offr., Grenada, 1921; do., Trinidad, 1921; do., Uganda, 1924; ag. senr. health offr., Uganda, 1929; med. offr., Zanzibar, 1930; tuberculosis offr., 1933.

FRENCH, Lewis, I.C.S.(Ret.).—Ed. Merchant Taylors' Schi. and St. John's Coll., Oxford; served as colonisation offr., Chenal Canal, Punjab, afterwards as dep. comsrr. and joint ch. sec. to govt., Punjab, 1896-1921; dir., development, Palestine, 1931.

FRERE, SIR BARTLE HENRY TEMPLE, KT. BACH. (1918), LL.B.—Ed. at Charterhouse schl. and Trin. Coll., Cam.; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1887; pres. dist. court, Cyprus, 1897; transf'd to Gibraltar as pol. mag. and coroner, 1902; atty.-gen., 1911; ch. just., Apl., 1914; judge, prize ct., Aug., 1914; cable censor during European War; ret., Aug., 1922.

FRERE, NOEL GRAY, C.M.G. (1934).—B. 1885; ed. Wanganui Collegiate Schi., N.Z., and Cranleigh Schi.; ast. dist. comsrr., S. Leone, July, 1909; dist. comsrr., Jan., 1915; ag. prov. comsrr., N. Prov., in 1921, 1923, 1926 and 1928; prov. comsrr., Jan., 1929.

FRETZ, WILMOT THEODORE STUART.—B.1888; ed. Framlingham Coll., Suffolk and Christ's Coll., Cambridge; Rhodesian admistr'n., B.S.A.P., N. and S. Rhodesia, 1913-19; Transvaal Border Patrols, 1918; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1921; atty.-gen., St. Lucia, 1923; chmn., agrl. comsrr., 1924; ag. admstr., St. Lucia, Dec., 1924; ag. ch. just., St. Vincent, July, 1925; res. mag.,
Jamaica, Apr., 1927; asst. judge, Zanzibar, Aug., 1934; ag. ch. just., 1935.

FRITH, GEOFFREY HAMMOND.—Served in the Great War; just. of peace, Turks and Caicos Is., 1919; ch. clk. to commr., olk. to leg. bd., sec. to bd. of educn., 1920; sub-insptr., pol., 1922; asst. treas., collr. of cust., postmr., gen. man. of savings bank, regist. of shipping, 1923; ag. asst. comsnr., mag., etc., 1927; ag. comsnr. and judge, grand ct., Cayman Islands, 1929; sub. treas., etc., Tobago, 1931; treas., St. Lucia, 1933; ag. col. sec. from Oct., 1933.

FUAD, MUSTAFA.—B. 1888; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn, 1922; ed. Turkish Schls., St. Paul's Schl., and English Schl., Nicosia, Cyprus; olk., treas., Cyprus, 1905; inspkr., pol. and dep. coroner, 1906; judge, dist. ct., Limassol, 1913; judge, dist. ct., Nicosia, 1916; mem., legal bd., 1916; puisne judge, sup. ct., 1927; pres., sheri. ct. of appeal, 1927.

FUGLES, NORMAN RALPH.—B. 1907; ed. Sir Roger Manwood's Sch.; B.S.C., Wye (Lond. Univ.), dipl. agr., Cantab and A.I.C.T.A., Trinidad; dist. agr. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Oct., 1930.

FULLER, HON. SIR GEORGE WARBURTON, K.C.M.G. (1919).—Elected to first H. of R., C. of A., 1901; re-elected, 1903 and 1906; min. of home affairs, C. of A., June, 1909 to Apr., 1910; col. sec., N. S. Wales, Nov., 1916-20; premier, 1922-25; agt.-gen., N.S.W., 1926-31.

FULLERTON, HON. C. P., K.C.—B. 1870; ed. Dalhousie Univ., Dalhousie, Nova Scotia, Canada; admitted to bar, 1896; judge, ct. of appl., Manitoba, 1917-31; ch. comsnr., bd. of rly. comsnr. for Canada, 1931; chmn., Canadian National Rly. trustees, 1933.

FULTON, ADAM, M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1897; lieut., May, 1915; capt., 1916; on active serv., Gallipoli, Egypt and Suez, France and Italy, 1915-18; demob., Jan., 1919; vety. offr., Gold Coast, May, 1926.

FURNESS, SIR ROBERT HOWARD, Kt. Bach. (1919).—B. 1880; ed. King William's Coll., Isle of Man; solr. (hons.), 1902; practised at bar of B. Honduras, 1906-13; regnr.-gen., B. Honduras, 1913; served with B. W. I. Regt., 1915-19; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1919; mag., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1920; senr. mag., Apr., 1921; solr. gen., Trinidad, Nov., 1923; ch. just., Barbados, Oct., 1926; do., Jamaica, 1936.

FURNNESS-SMITH, CECIL, Barrister-at-Law.—B. 1890; ed. Birkenhead Schl. and St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1912; LL.B., 1913; asst. dist. comsnr., G. Coast, Apr., 1914; dist. comsnr., 1921; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1922; crown coun., Mar., 1925; ag. solr.-gen., May-Oct., 1927; ag. circuit judge, 1929; solr.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, Aug., 1932; ag. atty.-gen. in 1933; atty.-gen., Zanzibar, Mar., 1936.

PURSE, MAJOR R. D., C.M.G. (1935), D.S.O.—B. 1887; ed. Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford, B.A.; asst. priv. sec. to sec. of state (Mr. Lewis now Lord Harcourt), Dec., 1910 to Aug., 1914; on inactive service in 1st King Edward's Horse, K.O. D.R., 5th Aug., 1914 to 26th Nov., 1918; served in France and Italy, Apr., 1915 to 26th Nov., 1918; promoted capt., 1914; major, 1916; wounded, 1917; D.S.O., July, 1918; Bar to D.S.O., gazetted, Mar., 1919; twice ment. in despatches, asst. priv. sec. (apptmts.) to sec. of state (Lord Milner), May, 1919; Mr. Winston Churchill, Feb., 1921; Duke of Devonshire, Oct., 1922; priv. sec. (apptmts.) to sec. of state, Mr. Thomas, Jan., 1924; Mr. L. C. M. S. Amery, Nov., 1924; Lord Passfield, 8th June, 1929; visited Can. on C.O. business, 1922, and again in 1923; at Imp. Forestry Confce; mem., bd. govrs., Imp. Forestry Inst.; asst. sec., Int. 1930.

GALEA, ARTHUR, O.B.E. (1930)—B. 1872; Malta Lyceum; ent. Malta civ. serv., 1891; olk., 1st Jan., 1896; 2nd cls. clk., July, asst. registr. cts. of judicial pol., Dec., 1900; registr., Jan., 1914; transf., secretariat, 1918; ch. clk., lieut.-gov.'s office, Sept., 1919; ch. clk. to legislature, Dec., 1921; char. charitable institutions, Apl., 1923; off. sec. head of ministry, Mar., 1927; asst. sec. to Apr., 1934.

GALIA, PROF. ROBERT V., O.B.E. (1883)—L.S. & A.—B. 1882; matric. (with hon.) M. Univ., 1900; graduated as land surv. and architect, 1903; lect. on engnr. and architecture, M. Univ., 1905; prof., ditto, 1915; ag. rector of 1923; el. for lat. div. in leg. assem., June; re-el., Aug., 1927; min. for pub. health, charitable institutions, Aug., 1927 and 1932, also min. for treas., Aug., 1929; leader constitutional party, 1932; leader constitutional party in L.A., 1932-33; rector, Malta Univ., 1934.

GALIZIA, HON. MAJOR JAMES A. C. (1933), O.B.E. (1924).—B. 1876; clk., Malta ser., 1893; ch. clk., P.W.D., 1905; man. wks. and elect. light dept., 1913; aspt. pub. and man., water wks. and elect. light dept., seat in exec. coun. and coun. of gort., M. treas., 1930.

GALLOWAY, WILLIAM CHARLES GOMBEY.—B. 1892; Lond. Institution of City and Guilds bronze medalist, telephony, A.I.E.E.; Br. P. engnr. dept., Jan., 1912; on active serv. (Signals), Nov., 1915; asst. telegr. engnr. P. dept., F.M.S., June, 1920; engr., Oct., 1923; sr. engr., P. and T., S.S. and F.M.S., May-1928, and Feb-May, 1929; sr. engr., Dec., 1934; ag. asst. engrnr.-in-ch., Nov., 1934.

GALWAY, SIR VISCOUNT (cr. 1727) GREVRE ABUNDILL MONCKTON ARNOLD C.M.G. (1935), D.S.O. (1917), O.B.E. (1918), B. 1882; ed. Eton and Christ Church, Oxford; Sherwood Rangers Yeomanry, 1900-04; Int. Guards, 1904; adjt., 1908; capt., 1911; capt., 4th Cavalry Brig., 1914; D.A.A. Q.M.G., 2nd Cavalry Divn., 1915; A.A. Q.M.G., 1917; brevet lieut.-col., 1919; Lieut. Life Guards, 1922-29; col. commdr., Hon. 4th Coy., 1933; gov.-gen. and commdr.-in-ch., New Zealand, 1935.

GALWAY, LT.-COL. SIR HENRY LANE K.C.M.G. (1910), C.M.G. (1899), D.S.O. (1888), B. 1859; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Sandhurst; entered army, May, 1878; promoted brg., Mar., 1881; capt., Oct., 1887; brevet-maj., May, 1897; maj., Mar., 1899; and lieutenant, Apr., 1901; apptd. dep. comsnr. and vice-coms. Oil Rivers prot., Mar., 1891; dep. coms. coms. Niger Coast prot., Jan., 1897; and dep. coms. Niger Coast prot. (now South Nigeria), Apr., 1899; ag. consul-gen. Niger Coast prot., to Nov., 1896; Jan., 1897; Feb., 1898, to Jan., 1900; ag. high-coms. South Nigeria, Mar. to Dec., 1900; Brass expdn., 1895 (desp., medal with clasps); D.S.O.; Benin expdn., 1897 (desp., clasps, bar majority); Aro expdn., as chief political officer, 1901-2 (desp., medal with clasps); govt., Helena, 1902; govt., Gambia, 30th Sept., 1914; govt., S. Australia, 27th Feb., 1914; govt., 18th Apr., 1914, retired, 1920.
HALWAY, JOHN PATRICK FRANCIS.—Ed. St. Anics Xavier's Coll., Liverpool; clk., vety. biological lab., Kabete, Aug., 1910; seconded, ly. serv., 1915; corp., E. African Vty. Corps., June, 1916; lieut., ditto, 17th Oct., 1917; ut., 3rd K.A.R.; "114-15" Star, Gen. Serv. d Victory med.; labour inspnr., offr., E. Africa Prot., Apl., 1919; office supt., P.W.D., c., 1922.

GAMBLE, FREDERICK CHARLES—B. 1891; Felsted and Wadham Coll., Oxford, B.A. (ons. jurisprudence) 1914; asst. dist. commr., A.P., Feb., 1915; transp. offr., N. Frontier it., 1916; ag. dist. commr., 1918; res. mag., ly., 1923; off. arbitr., Mombasa town planning beme, 1929; judge, high ct., Uganda and mem., of appl. for Eastern Africa, 1936.

GAMBLE, JOSEPH SAMUEL—Ag. sub-inspnr., B. Guiana, 1905; sub-inspnr. pol., 1906; vte musketry certif., 1908; dist. inspnr. gen., 12; county inspnr., 1920; ag. dep. inspnr. gen. nd sup't, fire brigade for various periods in 1920, 22, 1924 and 1926; inspnr.-gen., pol., Fiji, and mmdt., Fiji defence force, Oct., 1927; nom. em., leg. coun., 1928; title changed to commr., sl., 1936.

GAMBLES, ROBERT MOYLAN, B.A. (Cantab.), R.C.V.S.—B. 1910; ed. Westminster Schl. King's schol.) and Trinity Coll., Cambridge (cl. nat. sci. triplos, pt. I in 1931); R. (Dick) Vety. coll., Edin. (C.O. scholarship) and Univ. of din.; vety. offr., Cyprus, Jan., 1935; ag. ch. sty. offr., June-Oct., 1935.

GAME, FREDERICK HAROLD ROBERTS, A.C.G.I. (1921), A.M.I.C.E. (1925).—B. 1900; ed. Taunton chl. and Imp. Coll. of Sci. and Technology, S. Kensington; ast. engrnr., P.W.D., Uganda, sept., 1925.

GAME, AIR VICE-MARSHALL SIR PHILIP WOOLCOCK, G.B.E.(1929), K.C.B.(1924), K.C.M.G. (1935), C.B. (1918), D.S.O. (1915).—B. 1876; ed. charterhouse; ent. R.A., 1893; capt., 1901; adjt., 902; major, 1912; air vice-marshal, 1922; G.S.O., 1st and 2nd grade, W.O., 1910-14; served, S. Africa, 1901-02 (despa., Queen's Med. five clasps); European war, 1914-18 (despa. six times); dir., training and organization, Air Ministry, 1919-22; commanded R.A.F., India, 1922-23; air. mem. for personnel on air coun., 1923-28; ret. list, 1929; gov., New South Wales, 1930-35.

C.O. after compet. ex. as 2nd cl. elk., Oct., 1901; sec. to comittee inquire into organisation of Crown agents' o. 1908; asst. priv. sec. to Lord Crewe, 1st 1909; sec. to Royal comit. on Mauritius, 1910; asst. priv. sec. to Mr. Lewis Harcourt, Nov., ag. 1st cls. elk., Sept., 1910 to Jan., 1911, and 1st Apr., 1912; 1st cls. elk., 12th Oct., sec. colonial blue-book comittee., 1917; 1st elk., 1st Jan., 1920; asst. sec., 1st apr., mem., W. African currency bd., 1926-1928; mem., Palestine currency bd., 1926-1928; col. audit, 1st Oct., 1928.

HARDING, SIR EDWARD JOHN, K.C.B., K.C.M.G. (1928), C.B. (1926), C.M.G. (1917) (1907).—B. 1880; ed. Dulwich Coll. and H. Coll., Oxford (scholar, 1899); 1st cls.
nods, 1901; 2nd cls. lit. hum., 1903; B.A., 903; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1912; apptd. after compet. exam., 2nd cls. clk., marine dept. of trade, 30th Nov., 1903; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 31st May, 1904; sec. to distressed colonial seamen comttee., 1909; ass't priv. sec. to Mr. Lewis Harcourt, 14th Oct., 1912; sec. to Dominions Office Royal Coman., Dec., 1912; ag. 1st cls. clk., 10th Apr., 1916; 1st cls. clk., 4th June, 1916; on military service from 20th Nov., 1915, to 9th Apr., 1916; sec. to comttee. for attlt. of ex-service men within the Empire, 1917; ag. prin. clk., 1st Apr., 1919; prin., 1st Apr., 1920; ass't sec., 1st Dec., 1921; ass't under-sec. of state for dominions affairs, 30th July, 1925; perm. under-sec. of state for dom. affrs., 24th Jan., 1930.

HARDING, SIDNEY WALTER.—B. 1896; L.D.S. (R.C.S.Ire.); house surg., Inc. Dent. Hosp., Dublin, 1925-29; demonstr., 1929-31; house surg., Middlesex Hosp., Lond., Mar. to Sept., 1931; dental surg., Falkland Is., Nov., 1931; served in Great War, 1914-19; R. Dublin Fusiliers, Leinster Regt. and R.A.F.; lieut., Falkland Is. Defence Force, 1932; dent. offr., Malayan med. serv., 1936.

HARDING, WILLIAM, B. LITT., LL.D.—B. 1898; matric., Malta Univ., 1912; B. Litt., 1915; LL.D., 1919; legal adviser to army, navy and air forces, 1929; judge, 1934.

HARDY, THOMAS JAMES.—B. 1900; ent. C.O., 3rd Mar., 1916; apptd. after compet. exam., ast.clk., 24th Apr., 1918; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; acctnt., "Discovery" comttee., Dec., 1926-Dec., 1928; cler. offr., higher grade, 5th Nov., 1928.

HAREVEN-STONEHILL, DAVID, A.M.I.E.E.—B. 1896; ed. privately and Univ. of Nancy (France); mil. serv., B.E.F. (R.E. Signals), 1918-19; served in occupied enemy territory admintr., 1919; tele. inspr., Palestine, July, 1920; ag. ast. engnr., Aug., 1933 to Apr., 1934; ag. engnr. in 1934 and 1935; ch. storekeeper, Oct., 1935.

HARFORD, JAMES DUNBAR.—B. 1899; ed. Repton and Balliol Coll., Oxford (hon. schol.); M.A.; mil. serv., 1917-19; ast. dist. offr., Nigeria, 1926; ast. sec., 1930; clk. of couns., 1931-33; ast. C.O., Sept., 1934 to Sept., 1936; admtr., Antigua and Fed. sec., Leeward Is., Sept., 1936.

HARGREAVES, GEORGE MCNEILL, M.B., Ch.B., M.R.C.P. (Edin.), D.P.H. (Lond.), D.O.M.S. (Eng.)—B. 1901; Univ. of Edin. and Univ. Coll., Lond.; ast. dist. med. offr., 1925; ag. govt. bact. and pathologist, Jamaica, 1926; med., offr., Kenya, 1928; health offr., schls. and med. offr., ophthalmic br., Hong Kong, 1934.

HARINGTON, GEN. SIR CHARLES, G.C.B. (1933), G.B.E. (1922), K.C.B. (1919), C.B. (1917), D.S.O. (1900).—B. 1872; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and R.M. Coll., Sandhurst; ent. 2nd Batt., King's Liverpool Regt., 1892; served on staff, S. Africa, 1899-1900 (despa. twice, D.S.O.); European War, 1914-18 (despa., bt. lieut.-col. and col., comdr., Legion of Honour, maj. gen.); instr., R.M. Coll., Sandhurst, gen. staff, W.O.; bde. maj., 6th Infantry Brig.; G.S.O.L., B.G.G.S., Canadian Corps.; M.G.G.S. 2nd Army; dep. ch. Imp. gen. staff, 1918-20; G.O.C. Army of Black Sea, 1920-21; G.O.C. allied forces of occupation in Turkey, 1921-23; Northern command, 1923-27; gen., 1927; G.O.C. in C., Western command, India, 1927-31; G.O.C. in C. Aldershot command, 1931; A.D.C. gen. to King since 1930; gov. and comdr.-in-ch., Gibraltar, 1933.

HARKNESS, EDWARD BURNS, C.M.G. (1922).—Entered treasy., New S. Wales, 1891; sec. to Premier's office, 1901-16; under sec., depts. of ch. sec. and public health, since 1916.

HARKNESS, J., L.R.C.P. & L.R.C.S. & L.R.F.P.S. (Edin.& Glas.), L.D.S. (Ed.), D.T.M., D.T.H. (Liv.)—B. 1896; mily. serv., 1914-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Sept., 1927.

HARLEY, JOHN A.—M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), certif. Lond. S.T.M. (with distinction), July, 1909; apptd. to W.A.M.S., Gambia, Apl., 1910; ag. prot. med. offr., Jan. to May, 1911.

HARMAN, WM. HENRY, M.B.E. (1935).—B. 1882; apptd., after compet. exam., olk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv. and assigned to science and art dept., 10th Apr., 1900; to bd. of agric., 6th June, 1901; transf. to C.O., 27th Jan., 1902; staff offr., 8th Apr., 1930.

HARMER, JOHN DANIEL.—B. 1876; ed. Linlithgow and Trinity Old Stratford Schls., Edinburgh Univ., M.B., Ch.B., Edin., F.R.C.S., Edin.; war serv., 1914-17; med. offr., N. Rhodesia, 1917; surg. specialist, Apr., 1928; ag. D.D.M.S., 1934 and 1935.

HARNETTY, LIEUT. EDWARD.—B. 1887; ed. Brompton Oratory schl.; capt., Lincolnshire Yeomanry; lieut., Sierra Leone Batt., W.A.F.F., 1918-21; passed lower stand. exam. in Mendi and Mandingo; ast. dist. comanr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1922; passed higher standard exam. in Mende; dist. comanr., May, 1928.

HARNEY, EGBERT EWART.—B. 1898; clk. to regis-gen., Antigua, 1916; 3rd audit clk., 1921; 2nd do., 1922; ch. clk., regis.'s office, 1927; comanr. for oaths, 1927; ag. regis. and prov.-marshal, Dominica, 1931; prin., treasy. dept., Mar., 1933; passed bar final exam. (Inner Temple) Dec., 1934; ag. mag., dist. F., May, 1935 to Feb., 1936; ag. treas., Mar. Oct., 1936; temp. mem., exec. and leg. couns., Mar.-Oct., 1936; ch. regis., Leeward Is. and regis. and provost marshal, Antigua, 1936.

HARP, AUSTIN BYERS.—B. 1908; ed. Blundell's; agrl. dipl., Cedara, Natal, S. Africa; agrl. dept., Nigeria, 1930; Jamaica constab., 1933.

HARPER, SIR CHARLES HENRY, K.B.E. (1930), C.M.G. (1921), O.B.E. (1919).—Ed. at Blundell's schl., Devon, and Exeter Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1899; called to bar, Inner Temple, May, 1909; cadet, G. Coast, Jan., 1900; astd., Ashanti field force, June to Sept., 1900; astd. dist. comanr., Sept., 1901; ag. ast. col. sec., Oct., 1904; ast. col. sec., Feb., 1906; ag. ch. ast. col. sec. and clk. of couns., Apl. to June, 1908; cantonment mag., Coomassie, Oct., 1908; prov. comanr., July, 1909; census offr., 1911; ag. ch. ast. and clk. of couns., May to June, 1912; ag. col. sec., June to Oct., 1912 and from May to Aug., 1914; astd., Togoland field force, Aug., 1914; sen. polit. offr., Togoland, Sept. to Dec., 1914; ch. ast. col. sec., Feb., 1915; ag. col. sec. in 1915, 1916 and 1917; ch. comanr., Ashanti, May, 1920; gov., St. Helens, Dec., 1924; assumed govt., Feb., 1925; ret., 1932.

HARPER, FRANCIS HENRY, M.B.E. (1920).—B. 1877; transferred from the service of the Royal Niger Co. as supplementary clk. to C.O., 1st Jan., 1900; conf. clk., Nov., 1912; deptl. ast., 1st Apr., 1922; sec., "Discovery" comttee., 1st June, 1928; ret., 1937.

HARPUR, ISAAC, A.M.I.C.E., Chtd. Civ Engnr.—B. 1885; P.W.D., Nyasaland, 1917-20; ast. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Dec., 1920; ag. exec. engrnr., various occasions, 1923-29; exec. engrnr., div. pub. wks. office, Dec., 1929.

HARRAGIN, MAJOR ALFRED ERNEST ALBERT, D.S.O., V.D.—B. 1877; sub.-inspr., constab.,
Trinidad, Feb., 1905; asst. supt., fire brigade, Port-of-Spain, Sept., 1910; sub. inspr., Tobago, divn., May, 1911; inspr., constab., 1912; senr. inspr., constab., Apr., 1934; dep. major-gen., 1936.

HARRAGIN, WALTER, K.C.(1935).—B.1890; barrister-at-law; elk. of the peace and sub-registr., San Fernando and Victoria, Trinidad, Mar., 1914; served with the army as temporary major; mag., Victoria, Sept., 1919; crown counsel, 1924; ag. solr.-gen., Apr. to Oct., 1924 and from Jan., 1925 to Aug., 1926; atty.-gen., Nyasaland, Apr., 1927; ag. judge in 1927, 1929, 1930 and 1932; atty.-gen., Kenya, Oct., 1933.

HARRIES, CLIFFORD LOUIS REEVES.—B. 1879; C.S.L.L.; entd. Transvaal serv., 1900; inspr., native affrs. dept., 1903; native commr., 1904; seconded to Tanganyika admstrn., 1916; dist. polit. offr., 1917; returned to Union of S.A. serv., June, 1919; mag., Potgietersrust, Apr., 1923; do., Ladysmith, Aug., 1930; do., Kimberley, Sept., 1935.

HARRIS, SIR CHARLES ALEXANDER, K.C.M.G. (1917); C.B. (1904); C.M.G. (1900); C.V.O. (1917); M.V.O. (1911), B.A.—B. 1855; scholar, prizeman, and Porteous medallist of Christ's Coll., Camb.; Tancered student in com. law, Linc.'s Inn, 1877; 12th classic, 1878; apptd. 2nd cls. elk., C.O., after open competn., 1st July, 1879; sec. to W. Indies Finance Comms., Dec., 1882; asst. sec. Sugar Bounties Confe., 1889; priv. sec. to Mr. Buxton, M.P., Jan., 1894, to June, 1895; and to the Earl of Selborne, June, 1895; 1st class elk., 1896; specially engaged in work connected with Venezuelan bdry. arbitn., 1896-8; prin. elk., Nov., 1898; sent to Paris, 1899, in connection with the Venez. bdry. arbitn.; conducted British case in Brazilian-B. Guiana boundary arbitn., 1901-4; mem. of comte. to inquire into organisation of Crown agents' office, 1908; ch. elk., 1st Feb., 1909; represented C.O. on advisory comte. of comm. intell., B. of T., 1900-17; mem. of managing comte. of Imp. Inst. 1909-16; gov. and c. in c., Newfoundland, Nov., 1917; assumed govt., Dec., 1917; ret., 1922; author of numerous articles in Dict. of Pol. Econ. on economic and statistical subjects, and of lives of various colonial govts. and statesmen in Dict. of Nat. Biog.

HARRIS, DAVID JOHN EDWARD.—B. 1897; apptd. after compet. exam., boy elk., G.P.O., 1912; on milly. serv. (R.E. and R.A.F.), 8th Oct., 1915 to 27th Feb., 1919; temp. employment elk., Minv. of Labour, 1st Oct., 1919 to 20th June, 1920; permanent ditto, 21st June, 1920 to 30th Sept., 1922; cler. offr., C.O., 1st Oct., 1922.

HARRIS, HENRY GLADSTONE BOLTON, A.C.S.M.—B. 1885; ed. Exeter Sch. and Cambourne Schl.; mines; inspr. mines, F.M.S., 1910; ag. asst. warden, mines, Perak, 1914; ag. warden mines, Selangor, 1920; ag. warden mines, Perak, 1923; warden mines, N. Sembilan, 1927; warden mines, Selangor, 1929; do., Perak, 1933; senr. warden, mines, and offg. tin restriction contr., F.M.S. in addn., 1934; tin control advr., Johore in addn., June, 1934.

HARRIS, HERBERT JOHN.—B. 1884; entd. serv. of Imp. Post Office, Jan., 1900; transf. to dept. of posts and tels., Cape of Good Hope, Nov., 1902; resig., Dec., 1907, and entd. S. Rhodesia tel. serv., Jan., 1908; resig., Jan., 1910; prov. postmr., S. Nigeria, Feb., 1910; asst. supt. posts and tels., F.M.S., June, 1913; seconded for mil. serv., Mar., 1918; 2nd lieut., Indian army r.n.r. of offra., unattached, Mar., 1918; 2nd lieut. Punjabis, July, 1918; lieut., Mar., 1919; released from war list, Oct., 1919; resumed duty, Kuala Lumpur, 1920; relinquished comen., L.R.O., Sep., 1920; contr. posts and tels., F.M.S., Oct., 1925; P. and T., S.S., Jan., 1929; do., Sport., 1931; asst. sec. for postal affrs., S.S., dep., Nov., 1932; dir., posts, P. and T. dep., and F.M.S., Feb., 1933.

HARRIS, PRECTY GRAHAM.—B. 1886; Bees Schl.; Law Soc.'s studentship, 1911; ser. with King's (Lpool) Regt. and 1st Bn. Regt., 1914-19; France, 1915-16; admin. cls. IV, Nigeria, Jan., 1919; anthropologist, Lond., 1932; dep. rea., Apr., 1933; na., 1934; officiating sec., N. Prov., Apr., 1934.

HARRIS, REGINALD HARRISON.—B. 1886; Lord Williams Grammar Schl., Thame; Coll., Lond.; war serv., France 1915-16; R.I. ster Fusiliers; lieut., E. Africs, 4th K.A.; M.C. ment. in desps.; tax duties, Taps., 1934.

HARRIS, REGINALD ROBERT.—B. 1886; Queen Mary's Schl., Basingstoke; elk., gov't. office, Nyassaland Prot., June, 1915; govt. gaz., since 1914; elk., 1st cycl., 1920; ag. ch. elk., secretariat, Nov., 1921; asst. treas., Apr., 1925; ag. sec. treas., in 1930 and 1931; ag. dep. treas., 1935 to Mar., 1936.

HARRIS, WILLIAM VICTOR, M.Sc., A.I.C.F.E.S.—B. 1904; B.Sc. (Agr.), Armstrong Durham Univ., 1925; Cambridge, 1925; Imp. Coll. Trop. Agr., Trinidad, 1927; taxonomist, dept. of agr., Tanganyika Terr., 1927.

HARRISON, AUSTEN ST. BARBE, R.I. (chtd. archt.), mem. of Town Planning inst., 1892; ed. Monkton Combe Schl. and McGill Univ., Montreal; archt. and town planner of communications, Greece, 1920-22; P.W.D., Palestine, 1922.

HARRISON, ERNEST, C.M.G. (1933), M.Iwa., B.Sc. (Agric.), N.D.A. (Hons.), lect. in agr., schl. of agr., Grootefontein, Cap., prin., schl. of agr., Cedara, Natal, 1920; dir., agr., Kenya, 1921; ag. dir., agr., Nov., 1922, and Mar.-Oct., 1924; dir. agr., ganvika Territory, 1930.

HARRISON, CAPT. HORACE DERNON, 1884; war serv., with D.L.I., 1914-19; France, 1918; twice ment. in desps.; headmast., grm. schls., Gold Coast, June, 1920; mast. tr. coll., Jan., 1921; inspr., schls., Apr., 1924; asst. dir., educn., for various periods.

HARRISON-JONES, CHARLES.—B. 1886; Reading and St. John's Coll., Oxford; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1907; asst. gov't. Colombo and Negombodists., July, 1909; Matara, May, 1912; on military duty, dist. judge Tangalla, Dec., 1919; asst. g. Matale, June, 1920; do., Nuwara Eliya, 1924; gov't. agt., E.P. Jan., 1929; gov't. & P. Nov., 1932; do., S.P., Nov., 1935.

HART, BRIG.-GEN. SIR HENRY HART (1935), C.B. (1919), C.M.G. (1918), Croix-de-Guerre French (1915),—Served in S. Afr. from W. lieut., N. Z. volunteers, 1907; cap. territorial force, 1911; major, 1912; N.Z. exp. force (main body), 1914; 1915; col., 1916; temp. brig.-gen. commd. territorial brig., 1920; ret. list, 1930; admstr., Western Sam was A.D.C. to gov.-gen., N. Z., times men in desps.
HART, Henry George.—B. 1894; served in African Mounted Riflemen, 1913-16; R.F.A., 1916-19; war serv., German S.W. Africa, 1914-16; constable, N. Rhodesia pol., 1919; sergt., 1921; lieut., 1927; asst. comnr., 1930; comnr., 1936; ag. comnr., pol. and prisons, on several occasions.

HART, H. W.—B. 1897; on mily. service in France and Flanders, Mar., 1915 to Jan., 1919; service in corps of mily. accnts., 1919-21; temp. C.O., 1st Mar., 1921; apptd. after compet. am. cler. offr., C.O., 9th July, 1926.

HART, Lawrence Hereford.—B. 1891; ed. incoming Coll., pol. probtn., F.M.S., Nov., 1912; st. comnr., pol., June, 1918; ditto, Selangor, Oct., 1920; ch. pol. offr., J. Bahru, Dec., 1922; asst. comnr., pol., Perak, Dec., 1924; ch. pol. offr., Malacca, Apr., 1928; 1st asst. comnr., pol., Perak, Mar., 1929; asst. comnr., pol., M.S. Riys., June, 1930; 1st asst. comnr., pol., Perak, June, 1932.

HART, Rupert Lancelot Leon, M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1885; ed. Reading Schl. and R. Veterinary coll., London; govt. vety. surg., N. Rhodesia, 1910-14; vety. offr., Uganda, 1914; served with African Forces in Great War, 1914-17 and Western Front, 1917-19; senr. vety. offr., Uganda, 1920; ag. D.D.V.S. for several periods; D.V.S., June, 1932.

Harter, Jean Denis Edgard.—B. 1879; d. R. Coll. of Mauritius; asst. mast., R. Coll., 1901; asst. mast., Victoria Schl., Seychelles, Aug., 1902; asst. mast., King's Coll., 1910; headmast., Victoria Schl., July, 1920; ag. dir., educ. and inspr. of schl., Seychelles, Jan., 1922; inspr. of schl., Seychelles, Jan., 1924; co. to bd. of educ.; local sec., Cambridge local exam.; ag. pvtc. sec., clk. to gov. and clk. o couns. from Dec., 1924.

Hartington, Marquess of; Edward William Spencer Cavendish, M.P. (W. Divn. of Derbyshire).—B. 1895; ed. Eton and Cambridge Univ.; hon. col., 6th batt., Sherwood Foresters; bvt. lt.-col., Derby Yeomanry; serv. Egypt, Dardanelles and France (twice ment. in desps.); attd., Intell., 1916 and served W.O. and Br. mission, Paris; mem., Br. peace delegn., Paris, 1919; M.B.E., chevalier, Legion of Honour; contested N.E. Derbyshire, g.e., 1918 and W. Derbyshire 1922; mayor, Buxton, 1919-21; J.P. Derbyshire; parly. under sec. of state for Dom. Affrs., 5th Mar., 1936.

Hartley, Brian Joseph, N.D.A., A.I.C.T.A.—B. 1907; ed. Loughborough Grammar Schl. and Midland Agril. Coll.; C.O. agrl. course, Oxford and Trinidad, 1927-29; dist. agrl. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Oct., 1929.

Hartnell, G. F. W.—Chief mechanical engrn., Uganda rlyw., June, 1918, and from Apr., June, 1922; comnr., July, 1922; ag.regis.-gen., July-Sept., 1922.

Hartwell, Charles Herbert, B.A. (Canab.).—B. 1904; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1926; attd., Kandy kach., Jan., 1927; attd., secretariat, Oct., 1927; office asst., N. Eliya kach., May, 1928; asst. ch. sec., Aug., 1931; office asst., Batticaloa kach., Jan., 1932; sec. to min. for lab., industry and commerce, Mar., 1933; addnl. dep. contr., lab., May, 1933; attd. to treasy. and sec., select comte on salaries and cadres comnrn., June, 1933; sec., headmen's comnrn., in addnl., Aug., 1934; seconded as sec., to Sir Alan Pim in Kenya, Oct., 1935.

Harvey, Cedric, B.Sc. (Agr.), A.I.C.T.A.—B. 1902; ed. Woodford Coll., Essex, Transvaal Univ. Coll. Pretoria; Imp. Coll. Trop. Agr., 1926; dist. agrl. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Oct., 1927.

Harvey, Hon. Sir John Musgrave, Kt. Bach. (1933).—B. 1865; judge of the sup. ct., New S. Wales, 1913.

Harvey, Hon. Horace, B.A., LL.B., LL.D.—B. 1863; ed. Univ. Coll. and Toronto Univ.; called to bar (Ont.), 1889; called to bar Northwest Territories, 1893; regis., land titles, Alberta, 1896; dep. atty. genl., Northwest Territories, 1900; judge, supt. ct., N.W.T., 1904; judge, sup. ct., Alberta, 1907; ch. just., Alberta, 1910; chmn., bd. of govrs., Alberta univ., 1917.

Harvey, Reginald James.—B. 1901; ed. Charterhouse and Exeter Coll., Oxford, 1920-23; 4th cls., hons., mod. hist.; St. George Schl., Jerusalem, 1923-25; supt., educn., Tanganyika Territory, 1926.

Haslam, John, F.C., M.C., M.D., F.R.C.P.E., D.P.H.—B. 1888; ed. Dollar Academy and Edinburgh Univ.; on overseas serv., 1915-19; ment. in desps., 1917; M.C., 1918; asst. to prof. of med. jurisprudence, Edin. Univ., 1919; asst. govt., M.O.H., Br. Guiana, 1921; govt., M.O.H., 1922; asst. dir., Bureau of Hygiene and Trop. Diseases, 1925; physician and bacteriologist, "Shell" group of oil companies, Venezuela, 1930; ch. med. offr., Barbados, 1933; dir., med. services, N. Rhodesia, 1935.

Hathorn, Alexander Anthony Roy, B.A.—B.1882; ed. Hilton Coll., Lancang Coll. and Caius Coll., Cambridge; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1904; admitted advoc., Natal, 1904; K.C., 1922; judge, Natal prov. divn., sup. ct., S. Africa, 1931.

Haughton, Capt. Harold Moffatt Swire, R.E. (Sp. Res.), B.Sc., M.Inst.C.E., M.I.Struct.E.—B. 1884; war serv., Aug., 1914-July, 1919; asst. engnr., S.S., Sept., 1919; exec. engnr., Sept., 1928; ag. sr. exec. engnr., various occasions, 1931-33; exec. engnr., L. Perak, Oct., 1933.

Haughton, Sydney Henry, B.A. Hons. (nat. sci. tripes, pts. 1 and 2), Cambridge, D.Sc., Cape Town Univ.—B. 1888; palaeontologist, S. African museum, 1911; asst. dir., do., 1914; senr. geologist, 1920; dir., geological survey of Union, 1934; pres., Geol. Soc. of S. Africa, 1925; Murchison grant, Geol. Soc., London, 1927; vice-pres., S. African Geographical Soc.; F.R.S. (S. Africa); mem. nat. and historical monuments comnrn.; mem. fuel research bd.; mem. Transvaal museum comtee.

Haultain, Hon. Sir Frederick William Gordon, B.A., LL.D.—B. 1857; ed. Montreal High Schl., Collegiate Inst. Peterboro, Ont. and Toronto Univ.; B.A., 1877; LL.D., 1915; called to bar, Ont., 1882; K.C. (Dom.), 1902; K.C. (Sask.), 1907; mem., northwest coun. 1887-88; M.L.A., northwest, 1888-90; leader, exec. comtee, Northwest Territories, 1891-91; premier, atty. genl. and comnrn., of educn., N.W.T., 1897; M.L.A., Sask., 1905-12; ch. just., Sask., 1912; chan. univ. of Sask., 1917.

Havenga, Hon. Nicolaas Christiaan.—Atty-at-law; mem., prov. coun. for Fauresmith, O.F.S. and mem., exec. comtee. for O.F.S., 1910-15; mem., Union H. of A. for Fauresmith from 1915; min. of finance, from June, 1924; del., Ottawa Econ. Confce., 1932; del., World Economic Confce., London, 1933.

Hawes, Richard Brunel, M.B., M.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.T.M. (Lond.).—B. 1893; med. offr.,
Kedah, June, 1923; prof. of medicine, King Edward VII Med. Coll., Singapore, Apr., 1927.

HAWKEN, H. E. A.—B. 1879; ed. pub. schls., Ottawa Colleg. Inst.; ent. civ. serv. of Canada as jun. clk., dept. marine and fisheries, 1901; 2nd cls. clk., 1908; 1st cls. clk., 1910; ch. clk., 1917; ast. dep. min., Apr., 1920.

HAWKER, CHARLES ALLAN SYMOUR.—Served European War 1914-17 (wounded); M.H.R., C'wealth of Australia, 1929; min. for markets and repatriation, Lyons' ministry, 1931-2; resigned, Oct., 1932.

HAWKINS, BRIAN CHARLES KEITH.—B. 1900; ed. St. Paul's Schl. and Hertford Coll., Oxford; B.A. (Oxon.), hon. mod. hist., 1923; cadet, Hong Kong, Dec., 1924; 2nd ast. collr., treas., June, 1927; ast. supt., impts. and expts., Nov., 1927; ast. head, san'y dept., Oct., 1930; dist. off., South, May, 1932; 3rd ast. col. sec., May, 1933; sec., economic cons., July, 1934; ch. ast. to sec., Chinese affs., Oct., 1935.

Territory, May, 1927; ag. ch. sec., June to Nov., 1927 and Apr. to Oct., 1928; ch. sec., Jan., 1929; gov's dep. on several occasions since 1927; ag. gov., in 1929, 1931 and 1933; gov., North Borneo, 1933; accredited rep. to Permut. Mandates Com., 1929, 1930 and 1931; joint-editor "Hand-book of Cyprus," 1913 and 1919, and author of "Mad Mullah of Somaliland," 1923.

JARDINE, ROBERT FRIER, C.M.G. (1928), O.B.E. (1926).—B. 1894; ed. Downing Coll., Cambridge; served European War in Gallipoli, Egypt and Mesopotamia; polit. offr., Mesopotamia, 1917; asst. divnl. adviser, Mosul prov., under Iraq govt., 1921; admntr. msptr., Mosul prov., 1923; on sp. duty in Europe in connec. with Mosul question, 1925; admntr. inspr., Sulaimani, 1925; do., Mosul prov., 1925; ditto, Basra, 1928; ch. inspr., land regist., sec., dept. lands and surveys, Palestine, 1936; author "Grammar of Baghdad Kurmanji Kurdish," 1922.

JARRETT, JAMES HENRY, K.C.—B. 1895; ed. Lancing Coll.; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn; H.A.C., 1914; served European War, 1914-19; asst. dist. commr., Uganda, 1919; seconded, judl. dept. as mag., 1922; mag., 1924; asst. atty.-gen., 1926; ag. solr. gen., May, 1927 to Jan., 1928; crown coun., 1927; atty.-gen., Grenada, 1929; ag. admntr. and ag. ch. just., St. Vincent in 1930 and 1931; atty.-gen., Bahamas, 1933; ag. ch. just. and O.A.G., 1934; dep. gov., 1935 and 1936; col. sec., Aug., 1935; O.A.G., 1936.

JARRETT, NORMAN ROWSTONE.—B. 1889; ed. Highgate and Exeter Coll., Oxford, 3rd cls. class. mods., 1910, 2nd cls. lit. hum., 1912; B.A., 1912; cadet, F.M.S., 1913; passed cadet, July, 1914; offr., cls. V, Feb., 1916; cls. IV, Jan., 1920; dist. offr., Mar., 1921; offr., cls. II, Jan., 1925; offr., cls. II, 1930; asst. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Apr., 1930; ag. sec. to res., Perak, May, 1931; ag. Br. advr., Trungguanu, June, 1933; offr., cls. I I, 1934; ag. under sec. to govt., F.M.S., Feb., 1934.

JARVIN, CYRIL CHESTER.—B. 1884; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; Rhodes schol., 1904; Wadham Coll., Oxford, B.A. (hon. juris.); LL.B., Cape Univ.; sec., ch. just., Cape Colony, 1907; admitted Cape bar, 1910; ch. clk. to atty.-gen., O.F.S.; prof. ass't. to atty.-gen., Cape Prov., 1921; crown pros., Johannesburg, 1926; atty.-gen., Natal, 1933.

JAYATNE, MERENNA FRANCIS DE SILVA, B.A. (Lond.).—B. 1904; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Feb., 1927; attd. Colombo kach., Mar., 1927; office asst., Matale kach., Jan., 1928; pol. mag., Jaffna, Mar., 1930; fice asst., Batticaloa kach., Mar., 1933; asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Oct., 1934.

JAYASUNDARA, LAYARD, B.A. (Cantab.), B.Sc. (Lond.).—B. 1910; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Mar., 1935.

JEFF, CAPT. JOHN.—B. 1896; ed. Glasgow Univ.; cadet, F.M.S., attd Chinese prot., Ipoh, Apr., 1920; passed cadet, Dec., 1922; asst. prot., Chinese Seribum, Dec., 1923; attd., cust. dept., Jan., 1925; offr., cls. IV., Apr., 1927; ag. prot., Chinese, Perak, Apr., 1928; ditto, N Sembilan, Jan., 1930; ditto, Selangor and Pahang, May, 1931; offr., cls. III., Apr., 1932; ag. ast. sec., Chinese affrs., S.S., Aug., 1933; do., S.S. and F.M.S., Jan., 1934.

JEFF, RICHARD HUDLEY ALLISON.—B. 1889; jr. asst. engnr., F.M.S. Rlys., June, 1913; dist. engnr., grade III, head office, July, 1915; supervmr. dist. engnr., July, 1919; on sp. duty in S. India, Aug., 1919; dist. engnr., grade II, K. Lumpur, Jan., 1920; dist. engnr., grade I, Jan., 1924; ag. sec. to gen. man., F.M.S. Rlys., June, 1928-Aug., 1929; sr. dist. engnr., head office, June, 1929; ditto, Johore Bahru, Feb., 1931; divnl. engnr., F.M.S. rlys., Aug., 1932.

JEFFERY, CECIL ALBERT, C.M.G. (1936).—B. 1888; ed. Clyde schl., N.Z.; ent. N.Z. post and tel. dept., 1908; cik., govt. house, 1913; pvt. sec. to various ministers, 1915-20; ch. pvt. sec. to prime min., 1926-35; elk., exec. coun. and sec. to cabinet, 1935; served with N.Z. expd. force.

JEFFERY, GEORGE, O.B.E. (1924), F.S.A.—Scholarship, R. Coll. of Art and Science, 1872; scholarship in architecture, R. Academy of London (1874); F.R.I.B.A., 1892; architect to Rt. Rev. Bishop in Jerusalem and the East, 1892; hon. corres. mem. of Imperial Institute of Arch. of Russia, 1897; local sec. for Cyprus Society of Antiquaries; inspr. of pub. wks., Cyprus, 1898; curator of ancient monuments, Cyprus, 1903; relinquished appt. July, 1919; reappointed curator of ancient monuments, Cyprus, Feb., 1921; author of "Summary of Architectural Monuments of Cyprus," "Cyprus under an English King," "Historic Monuments of Cyprus," and of several papers on the medieval archaeology of Cyprus and Jerusalem, edr., new edition (1929) of "An attempt at a Bibliography of Cyprus."

JEFFREY, PAT COMMIR, A., R.D., R.N.R.—B. 1892; ed. Glas. Univ.; R.N., 1914-19; probationer, N. Rhodesia, 1919; J.P., 1920; clk. of ct. and under-sheriff, Batoka dist., 1920; asst. nat. commr., 1921; nat. commr., 1926; passed higher Chinyanga; asst. dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory 1927; ast. sec'y., Jan., 1930; ag. ast. ch. sec., 1934-35; clk., exec. and leg. couns., 1935; admntr. offr., 1st gr., Zanzibar, Aug., 1935; ast. sec'y., clk., leg. coun., edr., gazette and treas. liaison offr., Aug., 1935; ag. ast. ch. sec., Mar.-Oct., 1936.

JEFFREYS, ROBERT SYDNEY.—B. 1888; ed. Cape Town (S. Africa), Bedford Schl. and St. John's Coll., Cambridge, B.A., LL.B. (1909), Barrister-at-Law (Gray's Inn, 1910); joined admntr. of N. Rhodesia, June, 1914; ast. native commr., and J.P., July, 1916; resigned to proceed on active serv., Feb., 1918; rejoined N. Rhodesia admntr., May, 1919; native commr., July 1921; seconded to secretariat, Nov., 1921-Dec., 1922; ast. mag., Apr., 1926; dist. offr. (grade II) with powers of mag., Apr., 1928; seconded as ast. to sec. for native affrs., Mar., 1927-Oct., 1928; ag. crown coun., Nov., 1928-Mar., 1929; ag. pol. mag., May, 1930; res. mag., Apr., 1936.

JEFFRIES, CHARLES J., O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1896; ed. Malvern Coll.; class demy., Magdalen Coll., Oxford, 1914; 2nd lieut., 3rd Wiltsire Regt., Sept., 1915; served in France, 1916; lieut., 1917; invalided from army, Nov., 1917; tempy. 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 27th Dec., 1917; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, 2nd cls. clk., 16th July, 1919; sec., E. Africa land stintln. selection board, 1919; ast. sec., E. Africa currency board, prmn., 1st Apr., 1920; hon. sec., Corona Club, since 1921; sec., comteee. on governors' pensions, 1927-28; ast. sec., 1st Oct., 1930.

JEFFRIES, CHARLES WILLIAM, F.R.A.S.—B. 1882; Computer, Royal Observatory, Greenwich, 1897; junr. ast., Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope, 1903; 1st ast., Royal Observatory, Hong Kong, 1907; chief ast., ditto, 1912; ag. dir. in 1915, 1920, 1924, 1925 and 1929; dir., 1932.
JEKYLL, Lieut.-Col. Sir Herbert, K.C.M.G. (1901), R.E., C.M.G. (1885).—B. 1846; lieut., R.E., Apr., 1866; employed under War Office and Trinity House in 1868 to 1870, and destruction of sunken ships, from submarine mining, and under G.P.O. in the telegraph dept., from 1870 to 1873, and 1874 to 1876; served in the campaign of 1873-74 on the G. Coast; priv. sec. to the Earl of Carnarvon, Jan., 1877, to Feb., 1878; sec. to the col. defence comte., 1878; sec. to the roy. comm. on the defence of Br. possessions and commerce abroad, 1879-82; specially employed to visit and report on the defences of Singapore and Colombo, 1883-4; sec. col. defence comte., 1885; priv. sec. to Lord Carnarvon, viceroy of Ireland, June, 1885, to Jan., 1886; sec. to roy. comm. for Melbourne centennial exhib., 1888; priv. sec. to lord-lieut. of Ireland, 1892-5; sec. to the roy. comm. for the Paris exhibition, 1900.

JELF, Sir Arthur Selborne, Kt. Bach. (1932), C.M.G. (1927).—B. 1876; ed. Marlborough and Exeter Coll., Oxford (extr.), 2nd cls., class. mods., 1897; 3rd cls. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; M.A., 1913; cadet, F.M.S. civ. serv., 1899; held various admin. and exec. post in Malay States, 1900-10; asst. gen. adviser to Johore govt. Jan., 1911; offr. of cls. IV., Jan., 1912; chmn., san. bd., Kinta, Pernak, Apr., 1914 to Apr., 1917; 2nd lieut., M.S.V.R., Sep., 1914; lieut., M.S.V.R., Jan., 1915; seconded for mil. serv. (lieut., general list), Apr., 1917; offr. of cls. III., Dec., 1917; tempy. capt., gen. staff, S. Stlttns command; attchd. gen. staff, W.O. (milit. intell.), Jan., 1918; H.M. Petroleum Exec. (sec. to Lord Harcourt's comte.), June, 1918; offr., cls. II., June, 1919; ag. under sec. to govt., F.M.S., June, 1920; dir., Malayan polit. intell. bureau, cls. I.B., Dec., 1921; mem., Br. Malaya opium comte., Dec., 1923; pres., estate health comn., Apr., 1924 (recd. thanks of S. of S.); sec. to, Jamaica, Oct., 1925; ag. gov., for various periods 1925-32; lieut.-col., local forces, Oct., 1927; ret. 1935.

JENKINS, Edward Enoch.—B. 1895; ed. Peterhouse, Cambridge, B.A., LL.B., 1922; M.A., 1927; called to bar, Gray's Inn, May, 1924; joined South Wales circuit; war serv. (France) 1914-19; lieut., R.F.A.; cadet, Nyasaland, Sept., 1925; ag. atty-gen., Apr., July, 1927; ag. asst. atty-gen., July-Oct., 1927; asst. regtr., high ct., N. Rhodesia, Nov., 1927; crown coun., Apr., 1930; ag. atty-gen., various occasions, 1931-36; ag. judge, high ct., 1934; solr-gen., Jan., 1936.

JENKINSON, Thomas Richard.—B. 1893; Cape Col. postal serv., Mar., 1910; postal asst., N. Rhodesia, Mar., 1914; postmr. various centres, 1915-20; ag. acct., G.P.O., 1925-28; survr., 1928; ag. depy. P.M.G., several occasions, 1927-33; asst. P.M.G., Apr., 1933; ag. P.M.G. and chmn., elec. control bd., in 1934 and 1936.

JENKS, J. C. A.—Ed. Bristol Gram. Schl. and Angers, France; awarded Croix-de-Guerre (Palm) 1917; Order of Saint Stanislaus with Swords (2nd cls.), and ment. in desps., 1919; colonial audit serv., 1920; asst. audr. in charge, Zanzibar, Mar., 1923; senr. asst. audr. in charge, Jan., 1926; mem., retrenchment and rev. comte., Zanzibar, 1927; Order of Brilliant Star of Zanzibar (5th cls.), 1928; senr. asst. audr. in charge, Kenya and Uganda rly. and harbrs., 1929; audr., Mauritius, 1933.

JENNER, Frank.—B. 1878; served in Cape Mounted Rifles, Bechuanaland campaign 1896-97; Aug., 1928.

JENNINGS, F. G.—Asst. dist. comm. E.A.F., Apr., 1919.

JENNINGS, Priscilla Henry.—B. 1896; Christ's Hosp.; col. audt. dept., 1926; asst. audt., N. Rhodesia, 1927; asst. audt., Mauritius, 1928; ag. audt., 1932.

JEPSON, Frank Price.—B. 1886; M.A., Pembroke Coll., Camb.; exhib., medalion sch. dip. in agric. (hons.) in entomology, Wraysb. Coll., Kent, 1906; trop. disease reserch student in med. entomology, Camb. Univ., 1910; assisted in investig. by L.G.B. on flies of infection, 1908 and 1909; offr. entomologist, Fiji, 1909; offr. visits to Hawaii, 1911; Sec., 1912, Java, 1913; asst. entomologist, (civ.), 1919; ag. entomologist in addn., July, 1920; Mar., 1924 and Oct. to Nov., 1925; offr., U.S.A. (termite investig.), 1929; dep. dir., 1936.

JERMYN, Lancelot Ambrose Scott.—B.A. (Oxon.), M.R.S.T.—B. 1886; ed. Trin. (greenwood and Keble Coll., Oxford; held Malay Coll., K. Kangsar, F.M.S., Oct., 1900; do., Northam rd. Eng. Schl., Penang, Jan., 1901; do., Govt. Eng. Schl., Johore, Feb., 1901; do., Anderson Schl., Ipoh, Feb., 1902; do., High Schl., Malacca, Sept., 1930; do., High Schl., Auckland, Sept., 1931; Thames High Schl. and Auckland Grad., N.Z.; ent. COLONIAL REGULATIONS.

PART I.—PUBLIC OFFICERS.

CHAPTER I.—APPLICATION OF THE REGULATIONS.

1. The Regulations* apply to public officers serving in the following Dependencies:

- Bahamas.
- Barbados.
- Bermuda.
- British Guiana.
- British Honduras.
- British Solomon Islands Protectorate.
- Ceylon.
- Cyprus.
- Falkland Islands.
- Fiji.
- Gambia.
- Gibraltar.
- Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony.
- Gold Coast (including Togoland).
- Hong Kong.
- Jamaica.
- Kenya.
- Leeward Islands.
- Malta.
- Mauritius.
- Nigeria (including the Cameroons).
- Northern Rhodesia.
- Nyasaland Protectorate.
- Palestine.
- Saint Helena.
- Seychelles.
- Sierra Leone.
- Somaliland Protectorate.
- Straits Settlements.
- Tanganyika Territory.
- Trinidad and Tobago.
- Uganda Protectorate.
- Windward Islands.
- Zanzibar Protectorate.

Note (1).—The Regulations do not in themselves apply to officers in the service of the Federated Malay States, but the principles of the Regulations are applied to such officers by the incorporation of the Regulations in the Federated Malay States General Orders.

Note (2).—These Regulations apply to the British Resident, Trans-Jordan, and his staff.

2. In these Regulations the term "Colony" includes any territory in which the Regulations apply, and the term "Governor" includes all officers appointed to administer Governments, etc.

CHAPTER II.—GOVERNORS.

A. Appointment.

3. A Governor is appointed during His Majesty's pleasure, but his tenure of office is as a rule limited to a period of six years from his assumption of the administration.

B. Salary and Leave.

4. When the office of Governor becomes vacant or when the Governor is on leave, other than full-pay leave, the person succeeding to the administration of the Government, if he be an officer in the Colony, shall receive half the salary of the Governor, and half the salary of his own office.

Should the person called to the temporary administration have been transferred from the Colony elsewhere, he shall receive the whole salary of the Governor, if available, but in that case he shall not be entitled to any portion of the salary of the office from which he has been transferred. During the absence of a Governor, other than full-pay leave, of a Governor, and after the embarkation of a newly-appointed Governor, the person is only entitled to the half salary available. Whether he may also receive half the salary of the office from which he has been temporarily transferred shall depend on the arrangements made for the substitution, and shall be decided in each instance by the Secretary of State.

This Regulation does not apply to European officers in Tropical Africa.

5. The leave of a Governor is regulated by special rules of local application; but in most cases the Governor may be granted leave with full salary, exclusive of entertainment or duty allowance, not exceeding six weeks in any one year. In the absence of the Governor from the Colony, the person administering the Government shall receive in full any allowance provided for entertainments or duty allowance.

6. If the period of a vacancy or of the absence of the Governor should exceed nine months, and there be any salary available, reasonable arrangements shall be made, with the approval of the Secretary of State, for the increase of the salary of the temporary holder for the period of excess.

7. A Governor on appointment shall receive half salary if available from the date of entry into the Colony. An officer succeeding to the administration of a Government shall be entitled to half salary from the day on which he assumes the administration. The officer whom he succeeds shall not be entitled to payment for that day in respect of the administration of the Government.

8. If a Governor is transferred from one Colony to another and visits England on his way, the Secretary of State is satisfied that the visit is unavoidable or in furtherance of the public interest, then, as a general rule the half salary of the office which he relinquishes, until the date of his embarkation, will be paid; but if such half salary is not available he shall, as a general rule, receive the half salary of the office from which he has been transferred. If no half salary is available from either Government, he can receive no salary.

C. Passages.

9.—(1) The following is the scale of allowances granted from Imperial funds to Governors, according to the usual term of years in respect of their passages from this country:

| Dependency       | Allowance |
|------------------|-----------|
| Bahamas          | £400      |
| Barbados         | £330      |
| Bermuda          | £350      |
| British Guiana   | £330      |
| British Honduras | £350      |
| Ceylon           |           |
| Cyprus           |           |
| Falkland Islands |           |
| Fiji             |           |
| Gambia           |           |

*In certain Dependencies the application of particular Regulations has been modified by instructions of the Secretary of State.*
The passages of the Commissioner of Somaliland and the British Resident, Zanzibar, are paid from the funds of those Protectorates.

(2) When a Governor is appointed for less than the usual term of years the question of the amount of the passage allowance to be paid will be decided according to the circumstances of the case.

(3) The scale of allowances shown in this Regulation shall be liable to revision from time to time as the Secretary of State and the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury may determine.

10. A Governor is not entitled to any passage allowance from Imperial funds when proceeding on, or returning from, leave of absence.

11. On the expiration of his term of office a Governor shall be granted a passage allowance in respect of the homeward journey of the same amount as that provided for the outward journey; but the allowance may not be drawn without the previous sanction of the Secretary of State.

12. A Governor who is relieved at his own request before the expiration of his term of office must provide his own passage.

13. A Governor transferred to another appointment before the expiration of his term of office shall receive such passage allowance as may be determined by the Secretary of State and the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury to be appropriate in the particular circumstances of the case.

14. A Governor who is transferred while in the United Kingdom on leave, other than final leave at the expiration of his term of office, and who does not return to his old Colony, shall receive the authorised passage allowance from England to his new Colony. If the usual route from his old to his new Colony is via England he may also be granted at the discretion of the Secretary of State a proportion not exceeding one-half of the homeward passage allowance from his old Colony to England.

D. Passages in His Majesty's Ships.

15. No passage in His Majesty's ships shall be given to Governors or other public officers at the public expense except on the application of the Governor to the senior naval officer on the station. The expense of the entertainment of such passengers will not be paid from public funds, unless the Secretary of State approves.

16. The expense for the entertainment on board of His Majesty's ships of a Governor or other public officer must be paid to the paymaster of the ship at the end of the voyage, and, if possible, before leaving the ship.

17. The scale of allowance for entertainment on His Majesty's ships at the table of the Captain or Commanding Officer is as follows:

I. For any Governor or High Commissioner whose salary is not less than £3,000 per annum exclusive of allowances, £4 per diem for the first seven days, and afterwards 2½s. a day.

II. For any other Governor, or for a Lieutenant-Governor, Administrator, or Commissioner, £3 per diem for the first seven days, and afterwards 2½s. a day.

III. For the persons composing the suite of Governors, etc., 2½s. a day for each male person above the age of 16; two-thirds of that sum for every female above 16; one-third for such of either sex as shall be between the ages of 7 and 16; and one-fourth for such as may be under 7 years of age.

IV. For other public officers 2½s. a day for the first fourteen days, and 1½s. a day afterwards: and the proportions with respect to age and sex as stated in the preceding paragraph.

Payment for entertainment in His Majesty's ships is to be calculated according to the dates of the first and last dinners taken on board.

18. When a Governor or other public officer is proceeding in a ship of war on a tour of inspection which requires him to disembark at various ports, the higher rate per diem shall in general only be paid for the seven days' entertainment following his first embarkation. If there are special reasons for repeating this higher rate, it must form the subject of special representation to the Secretary of State before it is made.

19. When a Governor or other public officer disembarks for the purpose of performing bona fide public service, and has not been able to give the Captain or Commanding Officer beforehand such information as to the days on which he will be absent from the ship as will prevent expense in preparing for his entertainment on those days, one-half of the rates of allowance above authorised shall be payable in respect of such absence, and each day in respect of which such half-rates are paid shall be counted as a full day for the purpose of computing the seven or fourteen days referred to in the preceding Regulations.

CHAPTER III.—Officers.

A. Appointments.

20. The Regulations as to appointment to public offices are directions given by the Crown to the Governors for general guidance and do not constitute a contract between the Crown and its servants.

21. Appointments to public offices are made by authority of His Majesty, and such offices are held during His Majesty's pleasure.
22. Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed in His Majesty's name by an instrument signed by the Governor and sealed with the Seal of the Colony. Other appointments to public offices are made either (a) by letter signed by the Governor or written by his direction, or (b) by a formal agreement between the officer and the Governor or its appointed agent.

23. Public offices are divided into three classes:
   Class I. Those of which the initial emoluments do not exceed two hundred pounds per annum.
   Class II. Those of which the initial emoluments exceed two hundred but are less than four hundred pounds per annum.
   Class III. Those of which the initial emoluments are not less than four hundred pounds per annum.

24. When a vacancy occurs in Class I an appointment may be made by the Governor.

25. When a vacancy occurs in Class II a provisional appointment may be made by the Governor to be reported to the Secretary of State for approval in the quarterly return of officers newly appointed to offices in Classes II and III.

26. The powers of the Governor under the two preceding Regulations do not extend to the appointment or provisional appointment of a person not resident in the Colony.

27. The appointment to a public office of a person who has been connected with the Government as a secretary, aide-de-camp, or otherwise, is open to objection and must not be made without prior notice to the Secretary of State.

28. When a vacancy occurs in Class III the Governor shall report it immediately to the Secretary of State. The Governor may recommend a candidate to fill the vacancy, but it must be clearly understood that the Secretary of State may select another candidate. Any person who is appointed to set in the vacant office shall be distinctly informed that he holds the office only until his appointment is confirmed by the Secretary of State under directions from the Secretary of State.

29. In reporting a vacancy in Class III, the Governor shall furnish in duplicate full particulars of the vacancy in the form given in Appendix I.

30. In the selection of candidates for vacant offices in Classes II and III, the claims of members of the Colonial Service will generally take precedence of those of persons not already employed therein.

31. Unless otherwise provided in the conditions of employment, the appointment of an officer holding a post in the service shall be subject to a period of probation in accordance with regulations approved by the Secretary of State. The Governor shall have power to terminate an officer's probationary appointment, at any time, during the period of probation. At the end of the period of probation the officer whose probationary appointment is terminated or extended, be confirmed in his appointment. The confirmation of an officer holding a post in Class III, or the termination or extension of the probationary period of such an officer, shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary of State.

32. The claims of officers for promotion will be considered on the basis of official qualifications and merit.

33. The Governor shall, save as otherwise directed by the Secretary of State, furnish annually a report on the form given in Appendix 2 on every officer falling within any of the following classes:
   (a) Officers holding posts in Class III with eight or more years' service.
   (b) Officers drawing £700 per annum or over.
   (c) Officers who are not included in (a) or (b) who are heads of departments, or who are specially fitted for promotion or for transfer in the Colonial Service.

The Governor's report to the Secretary of State shall not be shown to the officer concerned except by the Head of the Department (or Reporting Officer) shall communicate his report to the officer, if it draws attention to faults or shortcomings which it may be desirable to amend.

The Governor shall also submit an annual report on officers on the active list of the Colonial Service, employment in the Colony, on whom reports are not made to the War Department.

B. Acting Appointments.

34. During the absence on full-pay leave of the substantive holder of an office, the person acting for the discharge of the duties of the office shall not involve any extra cost to public funds, unless:
   (a) where the Secretary of State has approved local regulations governing the payment of such costs, or
   (b) in very special circumstances with the approval of the Secretary of State.

35. When an office is vacant in a Colony for any reason other than the absence on full-pay leave of the person appointed to act in that office shall be remunerated as follows:
   (1) When the person appointed is not in the public service he shall be remunerated at such rate as the Governor may decide, but not exceeding the initial emoluments of the office.
   (2) When he is the holder of another office but is not required to discharge the duties of the office while acting:
      (a) If his substantive emoluments are not less than the minimum emoluments of the office he is acting, he shall continue to receive the former;
      (b) Otherwise he shall receive half the initial salary of the office in addition to the initial salary of his substantive office, and all the increments payable on the substantive office, and any personal allowance to which he may be entitled shall not receive in all more than the minimum emoluments of the substantive office.
   (3) When he is the holder of another office and is required to discharge the duties of the office in addition:
      (i) If the offices are distinct and separate offices in different Departments, he shall receive the initial emoluments of the office in which he is acting and the initial emoluments of the office;
Otherwise he shall be remunerated as though his case fell under section 2 of this Regulation.

C. Seniority.

Except where otherwise provided seniority as between persons selected for appointment from outside Colony shall be determined by the date of arrival in the Colony. Where, however, two or more persons from outside the Colonial Service arrive on the same date seniority inter se shall be determined by the letter from the Colonial Office confirming the selection, or, in the case of officers engaged on ent, by the date of the agreement. Seniority in any department shall be determined by the date of officer's appointment to the particular class or grade in which he is serving.

D. Salaries and Allowances.

On appointment to an office of a person not within the Colony, as a general rule half salary shall be from the date of embarkation, and full salary from the date of arrival in the Colony, provided that the proceeds direct to the Colony to which he is appointed; otherwise he shall be paid half salary for such as is ordinarily required to perform the journey between the port of embarkation and that of arrival Colony.

If the appointment of an officer who is acting in a vacant office is confirmed, he shall receive the full of that office, if available, from the date on which he entered on the duties, but from the date from which gives such full salary he shall not be entitled to salary on account of any other office which he may have the same time.

An officer who is promoted in the ordinary course in the Colony in which he is serving shall be eligible receive the salary of his new scale, grade, or office, if it be available, as from the date when the vacancy ed, even if he is on leave of absence at the date in question.

When the salary of an office is on an incremental scale, the holder shall not be entitled to draw any ment as of right, but only by sanction of the Governor. In the case of an officer (not being the head of rtment) a certificate shall be required from the head of his department that he has discharged his duties efficiency, diligence, and fidelity.

Except as otherwise provided an officer's incremental date shall be the date on which he takes up his tment in the Colony.

Except in a case of promotion from a non-pensionable to a pensionable office, the following rules shall when an officer is promoted in the ordinary course in the Colony in which he is serving to an office carrying on an incremental scale:

(i) If immediately prior to his promotion the salary of the officer was less than the minimum of the new office, he shall receive the minimum; but if he was qualifying for increment in his former office and had already earned such an amount of increment as would bring his salary up to the minimum of the scale of his new office, then any balance of the increment in his former scale shall, subject to rule (iv), be taken into account in fixing the date of his first increment in his new scale.

(ii) If his salary was not less than the minimum of the new office he shall, subject to rules (iii) and (iv), continue to receive his existing salary until by length of service at his new incremental rate he has earned such an amount of increment as will bring him to the next higher incremental step in his new scale. But, if he was qualifying for increment in his former office, the date of increment in his new scale shall, subject to rule (iv), be advanced proportionately even though it may mean the immediate grant of one increment and the advancement of the normal date for a further increment.

(iii) If the maximum (or fixed) salary of his former office was not less than the minimum of his new office and he has at the date of his promotion served at that salary for a period exceeding one year, then one-half of such excess period shall, subject to rule (iv), count towards an increment in his new scale, but in no case shall he be given more than one increment on this account.

(iv) If his former office was one to which no duty, seniority, or similar non-pensionable allowance was attached, and he is promoted to an office carrying such allowance, he shall serve for a full incremental period in the new office before becoming eligible for an increment.

When an officer receives, in addition to the salary of his office, an allowance granted to himself personally, not permanently attached to his office, he may when absent on half-pay leave receive only half of such allow ance, the remaining moiety being left undrawn and lapsing to the Colonial Treasury.
